messages.subject: [Fwd: Re: [DIST-SAMP] overfitting in DSM]
parts:
Rob,

Some thoughts on this problem below, but most of this reply will require
you to tap into R directly (I'm not very familiar with the DSM engine)...

You could also try rescaling your lat and lon values (if you haven't
already) so that they represent the same distance in each direction and
use an isotropic smoother. I would try 'soap' which is a bit more work
as you'll have to specify the boundary, but the examples are useful and
easy to follow (tip: use locator() and manually click round the boundary
if your boundary is quite high resolution - problems can occur if your
boundary is too detailed). In any case, using the soap-film smoother
might help with your unreasonably high edge values. What error
distribution are you using? It might be worth trying the Tweedie
distribution which is readily available in mgcv, and experiment with
the p-parameter. (See ?Tweedie within the mgcv package for more details.)

Is your 'ice' value a concentration, or a 'distance from'? Are you
hitting problems due to latitude and ice essentially measuring the same
thing? I wonder about trying a tensor product of te(ice, lon)... (given
that you probably want 'ice' in your model, and not just spatial
co-ordinates?)

In summary, this sort of thing is not necessarily a problem just due to
overfitting... check you are fitting a half-decent model as well! :-)

Some (perhaps useful) things to help with this, which I use fairly
routinely (but still don't always get a good model fit!):

(1) 'gam.check' within mgcv
(2) Choice of k: value not too critical as the smoothing parameters
control the model complexity, BUT if too small you will oversmooth, and
if too large, then computations may take too long. Quick check on
whether you've chosen a large enough k is to extract the deviance
residuals from the full model, and to smooth these w.r.t. x using a
Normal model and larger k. If the smooth picks up a pattern in the
residuals, then k should be increased in the original model. (See
'choose.k' in mgcv)
(3) usual residual checking (plot(model,residuals=T) and residuals(model) )

Cheers,
Sharon.



Rob Williams wrote:
> > Hi all,I am fitting a spatial model in Distance 6.0 (Release 2). I'd like to fit a model of the form
> > ~te(lon,lat)+s(ice)
> > The model appears to be overfitting. It's very wiggly, and is predicting unreasonably high density at the edges of the survey area where ice concentration is very high or very low.
> > Is there a way to call "gamma=1.4" in dsm within Distance to avoid overfitting? (I'm getting "unused argument" or "unexpected ",") error messages, so I definitely have the syntax wrong if it is.) Does this argument require me to run dsm in R?
